title: Conformance (OP) Pack Artifacts fails - tar file changed as we read it
signature: tar file changed as we read it|Configuration

failed_jobs.name: Conformance (OP)
failed_jobs.symptom: Pack Conformance Artifacts step exits with code 1 due to tar writing output file into the directory being archived

key_errors: tar: conformance_artifacts.tar.gz: file changed as we read it
root_cause: The 'Pack Conformance Artifacts' step runs: `tar -cvf - * | pigz > ${CONFORMANCE_ARTIFACTS_DIR}/conformance_artifacts.tar.gz`. This creates the output file inside the same directory being archived (the glob `*` matches the output .tar.gz as it is being written). `tar` detects the file changing mid-read, prints 'file changed as we read it', and exits with a non-zero return code (1), which fails the step.
reproduction_steps: Run: cd /some/dir && tar -cvf - * | pigz > /some/dir/output.tar.gz — tar will fail because the output file is inside the source directory.
recommended_actions: Write the tar output to a location outside the source directory: e.g., `tar -cvf - * | pigz > /tmp/conformance_artifacts.tar.gz && mv /tmp/conformance_artifacts.tar.gz ${CONFORMANCE_ARTIFACTS_DIR}/conformance_artifacts.tar.gz`
Alternatively, exclude the output file: `tar --exclude=conformance_artifacts.tar.gz -cvf - * | pigz > ${CONFORMANCE_ARTIFACTS_DIR}/conformance_artifacts.tar.gz`
prevention_strategies: When using tar with a glob or directory argument, always write the output to a path outside the source tree, or use --exclude to skip the output file. Add a CI lint check for this pattern.
historical_context: New pattern, not previously seen in the CI Doctor MQ database.
